description: Turn your coding agents into research agents
readmeExcerpt:
OpenResearch

The local-first harness & workspace for research agents.

an alphaXiv project

English · Español · 한국어 · 简体中文 · 日本語

Whether you’re looking for a copilot or an autoresearch tool, OpenResearch will accelerate your work. Launch research agents that can review literature, develop hypotheses, run experiments, and produce research artifacts.

macOS 11+ · Windows beta requires Git for Windows · Linux app needs glibc 2.35+

## Get started **We recommend using the OpenResearch desktop app.** Download it for your platform: - [macOS](https://github.com/alphaXiv/OpenResearch/releases/latest/download/OpenResearch.dmg) - [Windows (Beta)](https://github.com/alphaXiv/OpenResearch/releases/latest/download/OpenResearch-Setup.exe) - Linux: [x86_64](https://github.com/alphaXiv/OpenResearch/releases/latest/download/OpenResearch-x86_64.AppImage) · [ARM64](https://github.com/alphaXiv/OpenResearch/releases/latest/download/OpenResearch-aarch64.AppImage)
Prefer the standalone CLI? Install on macOS or Linux ```sh curl -LsSf https://openresearch.sh/install.sh | sh orx up ``` `orx up` opens the local dashboard at `http://127.0.0.1:4791`. On a managed Mac, device-management policies may block the CLI installed by `install.sh` because it is not yet signed. Use the signed and notarized desktop app instead. You can also install `orx` for your terminal from the app's Settings → Updates → **Install the `orx` command**.
Create an account at [openresearch.sh](https://openresearch.sh) to receive email updates and use managed OpenResearch compute. ## How it works **Use your favorite coding agent.** OpenResearch works natively with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, and Google Antigravity. You can also [use a local model](docs/local-models.md) with OpenCode through LM Studio, oMLX, Ollama, or a custom endpoint. **Ground research hypotheses in the latest literature.** OpenResearch integrates with alphaXiv, bioRxiv, and PubMed so agents can find relevant papers, develop informed hypotheses, and connect their experiments to existing research. **Choose your compute.** Run experiments locally or use SSH, Slurm, Kubernetes, Modal, Tinker, Ray, Hugging Face Jobs, and managed OpenResearch compute. **Give agents a memory of every experiment.** OpenResearch records every experiment in a local SQL database and keeps its logs, code, and artifacts on your machine so that agents can learn from past results and decide what to try next. The desktop app makes it easy to see what your agents have done and inspect the evidence behind each result. **Keep and own your research.** Run entirely locally. We don't collect your code or agent traces. Your projects, conversations, experiments, logs, and artifacts stay on your machine, under your control. ## Usage analytics Official release builds send opt-out, coarse product analytics events and detailed agent feedback in the background tied to a random installation ID. Your code, prompts, file contents or paths, repository names, tokens, emails, or project and experiment identifiers are not collected. Anonymized token/message counts are used to identify which models are being used across OpenResearch and can be seen at https://openresearch.sh/rankings. Feedback reports from the agent are sent for bug reports, feature requests, and general frustrations about OpenResearch. Agents are instructed to sanitize reports to exclude any sensitive information about your research or code. You can turn off all usage analytics and agent feedback in the desktop app's Settings or with `orx telemetry off`.

OpenResearch

The local-first harness & workspace for research agents.

an alphaXiv project

English · Español · 한국어 · 简体中文 · 日本語

Whether you’re looking for a copilot or an autoresearch tool, OpenResearch will accelerate your work. Launch research agents that can review literature, develop hypotheses, run experiments, and produce research artifacts.

macOS 11+ · Windows beta requires Git for Windows · Linux app needs glibc 2.35+

Get started

We recommend using the OpenResearch desktop app. Download it for your platform:

  • macOS
  • Windows (Beta)
  • Linux: x86_64 · ARM64
Prefer the standalone CLI? Install on macOS or Linux 
curl -LsSf https://openresearch.sh/install.sh | sh
orx up

orx up opens the local dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:4791.

On a managed Mac, device-management policies may block the CLI installed by install.sh because it is not yet signed. Use the signed and notarized desktop app instead. You can also install orx for your terminal from the app's Settings → Updates → Install the orx command.

Create an account at openresearch.sh to receive email updates and use managed OpenResearch compute.

How it works

Use your favorite coding agent. OpenResearch works natively with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor, and Google Antigravity. You can also use a local model with OpenCode through LM Studio, oMLX, Ollama, or a custom endpoint.

Ground research hypotheses in the latest literature. OpenResearch integrates with alphaXiv, bioRxiv, and PubMed so agents can find relevant papers, develop informed hypotheses, and connect their experiments to existing research.

Choose your compute. Run experiments locally or use SSH, Slurm, Kubernetes, Modal, Tinker, Ray, Hugging Face Jobs, and managed OpenResearch compute.

Give agents a memory of every experiment. OpenResearch records every experiment in a local SQL database and keeps its logs, code, and artifacts on your machine so that agents can learn from past results and decide what to try next. The desktop app makes it easy to see what your agents have done and inspect the evidence behind each result.

Keep and own your research. Run entirely locally. We don't collect your code or agent traces. Your projects, conversations, experiments, logs, and artifacts stay on your machine, under your control.

Usage analytics

Official release builds send opt-out, coarse product analytics events and detailed agent feedback in the background tied to a random installation ID. Your code, prompts, file contents or paths, repository names, tokens, emails, or project and experiment identifiers are not collected. Anonymized token/message counts are used to identify which models are being used across OpenResearch and can be seen at https://openresearch.sh/rankings. Feedback reports from the agent are sent for bug reports, feature requests, and general frustrations about OpenResearch. Agents are instructed to sanitize reports to exclude any sensitive information about your research or code.

You can turn off all usage analytics and agent feedback in the desktop app's Settings or with orx telemetry off.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A local-first workspace turning AI models into autonomous research agents for literature review and experimentation.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: OpenResearch provides a localized environment to transform models like Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode into fully capable research agents. It tackles the complexities of managing autonomous AI workflows by providing a structured dashboard and CLI tools. The platform enables these agents to autonomously conduct literature reviews, formulate hypotheses, execute experiments, and generate comprehensive research artifacts. It prioritizes a local-first architecture, allowing users to run workflows securely on their own hardware while offering flexible integrations with custom local models. This approach ensures data privacy and reduces dependency on external cloud processing for sensitive research tasks.
keyFeatures: Local-first architecture: Runs the primary workspace and dashboard directly on local hardware to ensure data privacy.
Multi-model integration: Supports transforming Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode into dedicated research agents.
Autonomous research workflows: Enables agents to independently conduct literature reviews and run experiments.
CLI management: Provides robust command-line tools for installing, managing, and launching local dashboards.
Local endpoint flexibility: Allows connections to LM Studio, oMLX, Ollama, or other custom local model endpoints.

useCases.title: Conducting literature reviews
useCases.description: Deploy an agent to autonomously scrape, read, and summarize vast amounts of academic literature on a specific topic.

useCases.title: Generating research artifacts
useCases.description: Instruct the AI to synthesize its findings and experimental results into structured papers or reports.

useCases.title: Running private AI research
useCases.description: Utilize the local-first architecture to analyze sensitive datasets without exposing data to external APIs.

useCases.title: Developing scientific hypotheses
useCases.description: Leverage the reasoning capabilities of integrated models to formulate novel hypotheses based on provided context.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Scientists, academic researchers, and developers seeking to automate complex research workflows using AI. Users should be comfortable running command-line tools and managing local machine learning models.
